scenario.summary: Threat actors use Microsoft Teams to impersonate help desk staff and persuade users to grant remote access via Quick Assist. From this foothold, they execute scripts via portable runtimes to discover and abuse AD CS configurations, specifically ESC1 and ESC8, to escalate privileges and obtain persistent domain access.

meta.rationale: Focus discovery queries on non-Domain Controller workstations. If the network logs are noisy, filter for connections originating from user-profile staging directories found in the portable runtime hunt.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is performing discovery against Active Directory Certificate Services to identify vulnerable templates (ESC1) or coercive authentication targets (ESC8), then obtaining certificates for privileged accounts to facilitate Kerberos authentication and data exfiltration.

hunt.name: AD CS Certificate Abuse and Lateral Movement
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the transition from initial host foothold to Active Directory domain escalation through Certificate Services (AD CS). It starts by locating workstation-to-DC connections on LDAPS and SMB ports that suggest template enumeration or authentication coercion. It then fans out to find evidence of new privileged certificates, certificate-backed Kerberos (PKINIT) authentication, and large data transfers linked to the same identities. An agent correlates these results to distinguish administrative activity from a persistent intrusion that bypasses standard password-based controls.

nodes.label: AD CS Discovery via LDAPS and SMB

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, LOWER(process_name) AS process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(*) AS connection_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE dst_endpoint_port IN (389, 636, 445, 3269) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{domain_controller_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{domain_controller_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY device_hostname, LOWER(process_name), dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port ORDER BY connection_count DESC
config.description: Identify workstations performing unusual LDAP(S) or SMB connections to domain infrastructure, indicating template assessment or coercion attempts like PetitPotam.
config.expected_signal: A small number of workstations making repetitive LDAPS or SMB calls to DCs. Silence suggests no automated discovery occurred during the window.

config.content: SELECT subject, issuer, common_name, serial_number, not_after, owner, provider FROM hb_certificates WHERE not_before >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(subject) LIKE '%$%' OR LOWER(subject) LIKE '%admin%' OR LOWER(subject) LIKE '%svc%') ORDER BY not_before DESC
config.description: Find certificates issued to domain controllers or administrative accounts within the lookback period.
config.expected_signal: Certificates for machine accounts ($) or administrative users not requested by standard automation. Absence on endpoints does not prove the CA did not issue them.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, device_hostname, src_endpoint_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, auth_protocol, cert_thumbprint, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (auth_protocol = 'PKINIT' OR (auth_protocol = 'Kerberos' AND cert_thumbprint IS NOT NULL)) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_hostname || ',') > 0) ORDER BY time DESC
config.description: Detect use of certificates for Kerberos authentication, which the adversary uses after obtaining certificates via ESC1 or ESC8.
config.expected_signal: Logon events indicating Kerberos with a certificate thumbprint, especially from identified beachheads. This is the primary indicator of certificate misuse.

primitive_config.expected: Logon events indicating Kerberos with a certificate thumbprint, especially from identified beachheads. This is the primary indicator of certificate misuse.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, dst_endpoint_ip, SUM(traffic_bytes) AS total_bytes, MIN(time) AS start_time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name, dst_endpoint_ip HAVING total_bytes > {{exfil_threshold_bytes}} ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
config.description: Examine network connections for exfiltration patterns, particularly from accounts or hosts involved in the escalation chain.
config.expected_signal: A user account with a newly issued certificate performing high-volume transfers to external IPs. Zero results is evidence of absence for the specific threshold.

config.objective: Determine whether any host identified in discovery is linked to a new privileged certificate or subsequent PKINIT logons for a different user/machine account.
config.description: Correlate discovery activity with certificate issuance and PKINIT logons to determine if a privileged account has been compromised.
config.expected_signal: A per-host and per-identity verdict citing specific network and auth rows.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per host, citing the certificates and logons.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for any host or identity

config.description: Route to containment if a certificate-based intrusion is confirmed.
Immediately contain the host beachhead and invalidate the issued certificates.
config.instructions: Isolate the compromised host from the network. Revoke every Active Directory certificate issued to the affected machine account or user account identified by the agent triage.

config.description: Review the agent's findings and confirm whether the activity was legitimate administration or an intrusion.
config.instructions: Examine the process that initiated the LDAPS/SMB traffic on the beachhead host. Verify if the certificate issuance correlates with a change request or a documented administrative task.

config.description: Record the hunt results and document any gaps in visibility.
